newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo firms see 1997 ind output rising 18 pct - IZIT.
newsitem.headline: Yugo firms see 1997 ind output rising 18 pct - IZIT.

text.p: Yugoslav companies hope for an 18 percent rise in industrial production in 1997, even though the government planned industrial output to rise by 10.8 percent, the Institute for Market Research said on Wednesday.

But in order to achieve higher growth rates, companies called for more credit support, further liberalisation of foreign trade, reduced fiscal burden and new cuts in customs duties, local and the so-called solidarity taxes, Slobodan Milosavljevic of the IZIT institute told Reuters.
"Even though those expectations may sound overly optimistic they may easily become true because the industrial production is still 45 percent below its pre-1991 levels," Milosavljevic said.

Yugoslav firms also called for more investment in fixed assets. Statistics show that those investments stood at 1.344 billion dinars ($265 million) and companies hoped for a nine percent increase in those investments during 1997.
"Those are insignificant amounts compared to six years of disinvestment," Milosavljevic said.
Upgrading outdated technology and equipment was one of the conditions set by foreign companies who wish to do business with Yugoslavia, he added.
The IZIT survey showed that only five percent of companies expected to increase investment by over 40 percent.
But 46.8 percent of 300 surveyed companies said they counted on a modest 10 percent increase in investments. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
